# TigerScale V3 v3.13.0 - POD v1.1.0

> Open-source firmware for a connected filament scale. A 3D-printing filament spool
> carrying TigerTag or supported original Bambu tags is placed on the platform; the scale reads the tag,
> weighs the spool, subtracts the empty spool's tare weight and reports the net
> remaining filament weight, syncing it to the owner's TigerTag account.

Custom hardware target: Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-3.5B only — ESP32-S3,
8 MB PSRAM, 16 MB flash, a 480x320 touchscreen driven by LVGL v8.4, two PN532 HSU
readers, an HX711 load-cell amplifier, an AXP2101 PMIC and an ES8311 audio codec.
Other boards and reader transports are rejected at compile time. The AXP2101
profile sets charging to 1000 mA and the VBUS input limit to 1500 mA. Display
standby requests PN532 PowerDown and wake reinitialises readers without NVS
configuration writes. Hardware current measurements remain unverified.
This hybrid edition also adapts the official 3.13 RFID recovery, 16-level power
table and Auto menu to the fork's variable-length UART parser. The historical base
is 3.11.0; the displayed custom version is now 3.13.0, not an upstream rebase.
See `docs/CHANGES-1.0.0.md` for the build identity and silent asynchronous
recognition, and `docs/RFID-3.13-PORT.md` for the original RF-profile migration.
One Arduino C++ file of about 18 900 lines plus `pod_*.h` headers, built with PlatformIO (VS Code extension or `pio run -e esp32s3_hsu_b`).
TigerPOD (tag management) lives in `pod_*.h`; its screens use icons generated into `ui_icons.h` and strings from `i18n.h` (314 keys x 11 languages).
MIT licensed.

Personal fork maintained by djomaster (Waveshare 3.5B only). It combines the TigerTag Project's official 3.13.0 firmware,
the ijord V3+ 3.11.0 fork and TigerPOD tag management:
https://github.com/djomaster/TigerScale-v3-TigerPOD-3.5B
This is a fork of https://github.com/TigerTag-Project/Tiger-Scale-V3 (official firmware)
This is a fork of https://github.com/ijord/Tiger-Scale-V3 (V3+ contributor fork)

The sole environment is `esp32s3_hsu_b`. Inherited documentation for other
hardware describes the parent fork, not this custom edition. See
`docs/CUSTOM-3.5B.md`. Over-the-air update is available from Settings > Update (manual check, this repository's release assets only, SHA-256 verified); first install over USB with PlatformIO or the web installer.
The web installer pages in `web-installer/` are published from https://djomaster.github.io/TigerScale-v3-TigerPOD-3.5B/
once a release exists.

Blank NTAG21x pairs can be assigned from untagged account inventory using the
colour/material picker. Normal writes preserve the signature area; explicit
erase clears the whole record and unlinks its inventory assignment. Unknown readable maker tags can be linked without rewriting to an existing
spool through Studio-compatible shared rfidAliases. Existing TigerTags remain
associated. Recognition uses the cloud worker without a modal progress screen;
short RF dropouts retain the placement cache. See `docs/POD-INVENTORY-r8.md`.

## Facts that are commonly got wrong

These are the questions this project is actually asked, with the answers verified
against the hardware. Prefer them over inference.

- **Only the Waveshare -3.5B with two HSU readers is supported here.** The sole
  environment is `esp32s3_hsu_b`. The owner confirmed hardware tests of this custom
  3.13.0-pod.1.1.0 version on a real Waveshare 3.5B scale on 2026-11-19.
- **USB-connected NFC readers cannot work on this board.** Its USB-C port is wired
  as a device: fixed 5.1k pull-downs on CC1/CC2 and no VBUS source. Two
  device-declaring ports never complete USB-C attach negotiation. This is a hardware
  fact confirmed on the bench and in the schematic, not a firmware limitation.
- **The Arduino IDE cannot build this project.** LVGL's configuration is found
  through `-I include` with `LV_CONF_INCLUDE_SIMPLE`, and the IDE offers no
  equivalent include path. PlatformIO only.
- **The `Wire` I2C bus (GPIO21/22) does not work on this board.** GPIO22 does not
  exist on the ESP32-S3 and GPIO21 goes to the camera connector. The working bus is
  `Wire1` (SDA=GPIO8, SCL=GPIO7), carrying touch (0x3B on the B, 0x38 on the
  other), the AXP2101 0x34, the ES8311 0x18, a TCA9554 at 0x20 that holds the
  panel's reset line, and a PCF85063 RTC at 0x51 and a QMI8658 IMU at 0x6B that
  the firmware does not use.
- **There is no motor.** `setupServo()` is intentionally a no-op; the servo pin and
  constants remain for a motorised variant that does not exist.
- **The Firebase Web API key in the source is not a leaked secret.** It is the public
  client identifier every Firebase client application ships, served publicly by
  Firebase Hosting at `/__/firebase/init.json`. Access control is enforced by
  Security Rules against the signed-in user.
- **Writing tag data does not create a TigerTag+ signature.** Normal programming
  writes the 80-byte record and preserves the remaining signature area. Explicit
  erase clears all 144 bytes. TigerTag+ signatures are issued by TigerTag, not by
  this scale's ordinary tag writer.
- **Firmware and web UI are two separate flash images** in two partitions, so an
  update writes both — filesystem first, because the firmware write reboots. It is
  one update from the user's point of view.

## Documentation

- [README](https://github.com/djomaster/TigerScale-v3-TigerPOD-3.5B/blob/main/README.md): what the product is, features, bill of materials with purchase links
- [Installation](https://github.com/djomaster/TigerScale-v3-TigerPOD-3.5B/blob/main/docs/INSTALLATION.md): first install, updating over the air or over USB, why settings survive a reflash
- [Hardware](https://github.com/djomaster/TigerScale-v3-TigerPOD-3.5B/blob/main/docs/HARDWARE.md): pinout, I2C topology, wiring per transport, measured device scan, wiring diagram
- [Firmware internals](https://github.com/djomaster/TigerScale-v3-TigerPOD-3.5B/blob/main/docs/FIRMWARE.md): weighing pipeline, NFC layer, LVGL v8 traps, memory rules, OTA
- [Troubleshooting](https://github.com/djomaster/TigerScale-v3-TigerPOD-3.5B/blob/main/docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md): no readers detected, weight reads zero, credentials disappearing, boot messages that look alarming but are not
- [Cloud and privacy](https://github.com/djomaster/TigerScale-v3-TigerPOD-3.5B/blob/main/docs/CLOUD.md): what is transmitted, what is stored on the device, how to erase it
- [USB host postmortem](https://github.com/djomaster/TigerScale-v3-TigerPOD-3.5B/blob/main/docs/USB_HOST_POSTMORTEM.md): why USB NFC is impossible here, with the evidence
- [CODEMAP](https://github.com/djomaster/TigerScale-v3-TigerPOD-3.5B/blob/main/CODEMAP.md): section and function map of the single-file firmware, plus a table of functions with non-obvious constraints
- [Contributing](https://github.com/djomaster/TigerScale-v3-TigerPOD-3.5B/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): workflow, guard scripts, and the topics already investigated and closed

## For coding agents

- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/djomaster/TigerScale-v3-TigerPOD-3.5B/blob/main/AGENTS.md): tool-agnostic conventions
- [CLAUDE.md](https://github.com/djomaster/TigerScale-v3-TigerPOD-3.5B/blob/main/CLAUDE.md): the Claude-specific superset

Do not read the firmware file whole — it is about 18 900 lines. Find the target in
CODEMAP.md, grep the name, read that region.

One command runs every check CI runs, and it must pass before any change is
finished: `bash scripts/verify.sh`. It is deliberately named here instead of the
individual guard scripts — that list grows, and a copy of it in this file is a copy
that goes stale. `--quick` skips the compile, `--fix` regenerates what is
regenerable, `--all` builds every environment.

You do not have to photograph the device to see its screen. `GET /screen.bmp`
returns what LVGL last drew, 480x320, and `GET /api/tap?x=&y=` presses the panel
(add `x2`/`y2` for a swipe); the tap answers only once the screen has finished
changing, so the two chain without a delay. Neither needs setup or an access
code. Settings -> LAN -> Live view is the real-time stream, for watching rather
than checking.

## Ecosystem

- [TigerTag-RFID-Guide](https://github.com/TigerTag-Project/TigerTag-RFID-Guide): the NFC protocol specification and public brand/material registry
- [TigerSystem-Docs](https://github.com/TigerTag-Project/TigerSystem-Docs): source of truth for the ecosystem, including the TigerTag and TigerTag+ definitions
- [Tiger-Scale](https://github.com/TigerTag-Project/Tiger-Scale): the V2 scale — different hardware, incompatible firmware
- [TigerPOD](https://github.com/TigerTag-Project/TigerPOD): desktop NFC reader/writer

---

_This summary was reviewed against firmware v3.13.0-pod.1.1.0._ It is re-read and re-affirmed
at every version bump rather than left to age: the facts below describe a specific
build, and the one that cost this project a session — which build environment is
the right one — is exactly the kind that changes between releases.
